dedupe_keys.name: daytime outdoor thermal comfort dataset for two public spaces in belo horizonte brazil 2013

description: This dataset pairs microclimate measurements in two urban open public spaces in Belo Horizonte with interviews of the people using them, taken during the day in summer and winter 2013. It gives air temperature, humidity, wind and radiation readings, the physiological equivalent temperature index computed from them, and each respondent's thermal sensation, preference and comfort judgement, along with personal and behavioural details such as clothing and activity. It was produced by Hirashima, Assis and Nikolopoulou, and the data were first analysed in a doctoral thesis on sound and thermal perception in open spaces in Belo Horizonte. Coverage: two public squares in one Brazilian city. Access: free as supplementary files of a 2016 Data in Brief article on PubMed Central. Licence: CC BY. Caveats: daytime only, two sites and one year; the comfort ranges are local and not directly transferable. Simulation uses are calibrating outdoor thermal comfort models such as ENVI-met and RayMan for tropical highland cities, and checking heat stress thresholds when redesigning squares. Related records: the ASHRAE global thermal comfort database, ENVI-met and the Leeds urban canyons temperature dataset.
